children: Italy needs to keep its public finances in check as the European Central Bank is raising interest rates, Economy Minister Giancarlo Giorgetti said on Sunday.

The ECB raised borrowing costs on Thursday for the second time this year and sources told Reuters policymakers expect further policy tightening in the months ahead, with a move possible as early as October.

"At times like these, with interest rates rising, it becomes clear how important it is to keep debt under control and to have the confidence of the markets and savers in order to place government bonds with investors," Giorgetti said, addressing a political conference in Rome.
